question.text: Which party will win the most votes in Spain's November 29, 2026 general election?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the party whose candidacies receive the most valid votes nationwide in the November 29, 2026 election to the Congress of Deputies, per the proclaimed results published by the Junta Electoral Central, the Ministry of the Interior or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), after any recounts.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the proclaimed nationwide valid-vote totals for the Congress election, as published by the Junta Electoral Central, the Ministry of the Interior or credible sources. No results exist yet because the vote is on 2026-11-29.
- 2026-11-02: Provincial electoral boards proclaimed the candidacies. Parties can appeal until 2026-11-05. [Cronista](https://www.cronista.com/espana/politica-es/las-juntas-electorales-proclaman-las-candidaturas-del-29n-los-partidos-tendran-hasta-el-5-de-noviembre-para-recurrir/)
- 2026-11-03: The BOE published the 893 lists that are running. [Europa Press ticker](https://ticker-noticiasep.microcontenidos.com/NoticiaRSS.vbhtml?user=2EH286PZLE&cod=20261103135600)
- I did not re-fetch the DatosRTVE average myself.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The election is 26 days away.
- PP leads every published private poll, including all six done after the train crash. The only polls putting PSOE first are the CIS (a state polling body that has favoured PSOE in past cycles, so I call it a "house effect") and a leaked internal Vox poll.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: The Sondaxe poll for La Voz de Galicia had PP 29.2%, PSOE 26.9%, Vox 19.2%, Frente Amplio 7.2% (1,200 interviews). Fieldwork ran 26-28 Oct and ended on the day of the crash, so it barely captures any effect. Narciso Michavila of the polling firm GAD3 is quoted describing an "abrupt change in vote" since the crash. He said it is now "impossible" for Sánchez to get the most votes. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/11/03/el-pp-ganaria-las-elecciones-con-23-puntos-de-ventaja-sobre-el-psoe-y-vox-seria-la-fuerza-que-mas-crece-segun-la-ultima-encuesta-antes-del-accidente-de-trenes-en-toledo/)
- 2026-11-01/02: Polls taken after the crash:

| ElectoPanel (Electomanía) | 31.5% | 25.8% | 19.2% | 6.2% |

  PP leads by 5.7 to 7 points in all six. [Electomanía](https://electomania.es/primera-oleada-de-encuestas-tras-el-accidente-ferroviario-te-las-resumimos-aqui/), [El Plural](https://www.elplural.com/politica/espana/primeras-encuestas-accidente-urda-frenan-psoe-impulsan-pp-vox_802968102)
- 2026-11-02: Sigma Dos (fieldwork 29-30 Oct) estimates PSOE has lost about 450,000 votes since the crash. Its research deputy director says the share of PSOE voters moving to PP rose from 6.9% before the crash to 9.5%. [COPE](https://www.cope.es/programas/la-tarde/noticias/ignacio-clemente-subdirector-investigacion-sigma-dos-accidente-ferroviario-hemos-observado-perdida-apoyos-partido-socialista-incremento-6-9-partido-popular-20261102_3467089.html), [UHN Plus](https://www.uhnplus.com/espana-psoe-cae-100-escanos-encuesta-sigma-dos-el-mundo-accidente-urda/)
- 2026-11-01: A leaked internal Vox poll has PSOE 29.6%, PP 28.1%, Vox 20.2%. It is not a published poll. [The Objective](https://theobjective.com/espana/2026-11-01/sondeo-vox-71-escanos/)
- First week of November: the Colmena de Datos polling average has PP 31.4%, PSOE 26.3%, Vox 19.5%, FA 6.4%. [Colmena de Datos](https://colmenadedatos.com/media-de-encuestas-elecciones-espana-1a-semana-de-noviembre-2026/)
- 2026-10-28: A train crash at Urda (Toledo) killed 69 people. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/11/03/el-pp-ganaria-las-elecciones-con-23-puntos-de-ventaja-sobre-el-psoe-y-vox-seria-la-fuerza-que-mas-crece-segun-la-ultima-encuesta-antes-del-accidente-de-trenes-en-toledo/)
- 2026-10-27: Before the crash, PSOE was reported to be "gaining ground". [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/10/27/asi-estan-las-encuestas-para-el-29-de-noviembre-pp-y-vox-mantienen-la-mayoria-absoluta-el-psoe-gana-terreno-y-la-izquierda-fragmentada-no-logra-remontar/)
- 2026-10-14: The October CIS barometer (5,025 respondents) has PSOE 34.0%, PP 22.2%, Vox 17.1%. Direct vote intention, before CIS's own adjustment, was PSOE 25.3%, PP 14.7%. [Moncloa.com](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/10/14/cis-octubre-hunde-pp-psoe-34-3448290/)
- 2026-10-09: The DYM poll for 20minutos has PP 34%. [20minutos](https://www.20minutos.es/nacional/quien-ganara-elecciones-29-noviembre-segun-encuestas-sondeos_7044112_0.html)
- 2026-10-05: Sánchez called the snap election after his housing decrees failed. [20minutos](https://www.20minutos.es/nacional/quien-ganara-elecciones-29-noviembre-segun-encuestas-sondeos_7044112_0.html)

## 4. Base rates
- PP or PSOE has come first in every general election since 1982 (14 of 14), with PSOE first 8 times and PP 6. Vox's best result is 15.1% (Nov 2019). Current polls put it around 19-20%, still about 5 to 13 points behind first place.
- Past polling misses relevant here:
  - In 2023 the final private polls had PP ahead by roughly 4 to 7 points. It actually won by about 1.4 points (33.1% vs 31.7%). Private polls overstated PP's lead, but they still picked the right winner.
  - CIS has repeatedly overstated PSOE's share in past cycles.
- PP's current lead in private polls (5 to 7 points) is larger than the 2023 polling miss on the PP-PSOE margin (about 3 to 5 points).

## 5. Other forecasts
These are market prices fetched 2026-11-03 15:09 UTC.
- Polymarket, "Spain General Election Winner": PP 86.5%, PSOE 11.5%, Vox 0.15%, FA 0.05%. This market looks like it is about the overall winner, not necessarily the vote leader, so check how it defines winning. It is still a close match. A placeholder option, "Party D", shows 0.5.
- Kalshi PSOE vote share: at least 27% priced at 0.43, at least 28% at 0.27, at least 30% at 0.14. Kalshi Vox vote share: at least 19% at 0.51, at least 22% at 0.11. Kalshi PP seats: 135 or more at 0.49.
- Polymarket PP-PSOE seat margin: every bucket shown is a PP lead (the price list is inconsistent and does not sum to 1).
- About 2026-10-15: the bookmaker Sportium offered odds of PP 1.10, PSOE 5.00, Vox 41.00. [Casasdeapuestas](https://www.casasdeapuestas.com/noticias/cis-apuestas-elecciones-generales-29n/)
- I could not find the Metaculus community forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-05: deadline to appeal the candidacy proclamations.
- Mid-November: the official campaign starts, televised debates are likely, and the CIS pre-election macro-survey is expected. I did not find exact dates.
- Spanish law bans publishing polls in the final five days, so the last ones should come out around 2026-11-23.
- Further fallout from the Urda crash investigation (accountability for the transport ministry), and how the housing unrest develops.
- 2026-11-29: election night, with the Interior Ministry's provisional count. The official scrutiny and proclamation of results come in the following weeks, before the 2026-12-31 resolution date.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the proclaimed valid-vote totals for the Congress of Deputies, published by the Junta Electoral Central (JEC) or the Ministry of the Interior. The election hasn't happened, so there are no results yet. Under Spanish electoral law (LOREG), the JEC usually proclaims results a few weeks after polling day, and the Interior Ministry's provisional count comes out on election night.
- 2026-11-03: The BOE (official state gazette) published the 893 lists proclaimed by the provincial electoral boards. Parties can appeal until November 5. [Europa Press ticker](https://ticker-noticiasep.microcontenidos.com/NoticiaRSS.vbhtml?user=2EH286PZLE&cod=20261103135600), [Cronista](https://www.cronista.com/espana/politica-es/las-juntas-electorales-proclaman-las-candidaturas-del-29n-los-partidos-tendran-hasta-el-5-de-noviembre-para-recurrir/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. Voting is on November 29.
- Almost every independent poll puts PP first. Of the last 15 polls on Wikipedia, only two show PSOE ahead, and both are partisan: a PSOE internal poll and a Vox internal poll reported by The Objective.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Colmena de Datos average for the first week of November: PP 31.4% (-1.2 from October), PSOE 26.3% (+0.6), Vox 19.5% (+1.3), Sumar 6.4%, Podemos 2.7%. [Colmena de Datos](https://colmenadedatos.com/media-de-encuestas-elecciones-espana-1a-semana-de-noviembre-2026/)
- 2026-11-03: Sondaxe/La Voz de Galicia, fieldwork October 26-28 (1,200 interviews, mostly before the crash): PP 29.2%, PSOE 26.9%, Vox 19.2%, FA 7.2%. GAD3's Narciso Michavila is quoted describing an "abrupt shift" in voting since the crash, but he gave no figures. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/11/03/el-pp-ganaria-las-elecciones-con-23-puntos-de-ventaja-sobre-el-psoe-y-vox-seria-la-fuerza-que-mas-crece-segun-la-ultima-encuesta-antes-del-accidente-de-trenes-en-toledo/)
- 2026-11-01/02: Post-crash polls (fieldwork October 28-30) [Wikipedia tracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2026_Spanish_general_election):
  - Sigma Dos/El Mundo: PP 31.1, PSOE 24.6, Vox 19.3
  - Target Point/El Debate: PP 31.8, PSOE 25.5, Vox 19.9
  - EM-Analytics: PP 31.5, PSOE 25.8, Vox 19.2
  - NC Report (October 26-29): PP 33.0, PSOE 25.6
  - SocioMétrica (to November 1): PP 32.7, PSOE 26.6
- 2026-11-01: A Vox internal poll published by The Objective has PSOE at 29.6% and PP at 28.1%, with Vox on 71 seats. Treat it with caution because it comes from a party. [The Objective](https://theobjective.com/espana/2026-11-01/sondeo-vox-71-escanos/)
- 2026-10-28: The Urda/Los Yébenes train crash in Toledo killed about 64-69 people (reports differ). Campaigning was suspended except by Vox, and the Transport Minister refused to resign. Coverage frames the crash as hurting PSOE. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/30/spains-train-crash-redraws-the-electoral-battle-ahead-of-the-elections), [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/en/general-elections-spain/29n-waits-for-no-one-the-tragedy-in-urda-forces-psoe-in-shock-to-reorient-its-campaign/)

- 2026-10-14: The October CIS barometer (the state pollster, run by Tezanos) is the outlier: PSOE 34.0%, PP 22.2%, Vox 17.1%. The CIS has a long record of favouring PSOE. [Moncloa.com](https://www.moncloa.com/2026/10/14/cis-octubre-hunde-pp-psoe-34-3448290/), [Euronews](https://es.euronews.com/2026/10/14/cis-psoe-una-subida-34-saca-casi-12-puntos-al-pp-a-mes-y-medio-del-29n)

## 4. Base rates
- PP or PSOE has won the most votes in every general election since 1982, 14 out of 14. Vox's best result was 15.1% in November 2019, and current polls put it at about 19-20%, roughly 11-12 points behind PP.
- How much polls miss by in Spain:
  - 2023: final polls had PP ahead by about 5-10 points. PP won by only 1.4 (33.1 vs 31.7).
  - 2019: PSOE's lead was close to what polls showed.
  - 2016: polls overstated Unidos Podemos.
  - The takeaway is that a 5-6 point lead has been cut sharply before. Polls overstating PP and understating PSOE is a recent, documented pattern.
- The current non-partisan lead for PP runs from about 2.3 points (Sondaxe, Winston) to 7.4 (NC Report). Most polls show 4.5-6.5.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket, "Spain General Election Winner" (prices as of 2026-11-03): PP 86.5%, PSOE 11.5%, Vox 0.15%, FA 0.05%. Check whether this market resolves on most votes or most seats. Its wording wasn't verified, though the two very likely go together.
- Kalshi, PSOE vote share: ≥27% at 43%, ≥28% at 27%, ≥30% at 14%. Vox ≥19% at 51%, ≥22% at 11%. PP seats ≥135 at 49%. PP+Vox combined ≥50% at 46%. These price Vox finishing first as very unlikely.
- 2026-10-15: Sportium bookmaker odds: PP 1.10, PSOE 5.00, Vox 41.00. [casasdeapuestas.com](https://www.casasdeapuestas.com/noticias/cis-apuestas-elecciones-generales-29n/)
- I didn't find a Manifold market or a published expert model with win probabilities.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-05: Deadline for appeals against the proclaimed lists.
- Further CIS releases: probably a pre-election survey in November. I couldn't confirm the date.
- Official campaign: under standard LOREG timing it should run from about November 13 to November 27. Poll publication is banned in the last five days (from about November 24). These dates come from the law, not from any 2026 announcement I found.
- TV debates: I found no confirmed dates.
- Crash investigation: any findings on the Urda crash and political fallout (the minister's position).
- 2026-11-29: Election day. The provisional count comes that night, and JEC proclamation follows within weeks.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The election is on 2026-11-29, 26 days from now. Provisional results will be known that night, and the official proclamation follows before the 2026-12-31 resolution date.

(b) **Status quo:** PP comes first in votes. It leads every private poll, by about 5 to 7 points after the crash and about 4.7 points in the DatosRTVE average (31.5% vs 26.8%).

(c) **Base rates:** PP or PSOE has come first in all 14 elections since 1982 (PSOE 8, PP 6). No third party has come close: Vox's best result is 15.1%, and other parties have never topped the national vote.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **Post-crash polls (2026-11-01/02):** Six private polls give PP leads of 5.7 to 7 points. Sigma Dos estimates PSOE lost about 450k votes after the 2026-10-28 Urda train crash.
- **Other polls:** The Colmena average (first week of November) has PP 31.4% and PSOE 26.3%. Sondaxe (fieldwork 26-28 Oct) has a 2.3-point lead. IMOP (13-16 Oct) had only 1.4 points.
- **Polls favouring PSOE:** The CIS (PSOE +12) has a known pro-PSOE house effect. The leaked Vox internal poll (PSOE +1.5) is unpublished.
- **2023 precedent:** Private polls overstated PP's lead by about 3 to 5 points, but still picked the right winner.
- **Markets (2026-11-03):** Polymarket has PP 86.5% and PSOE 11.5%. Its contract is about the "winner", so it is a close but not exact match to the most-votes criterion. Kalshi PSOE ≥28% is priced at 0.27.

(e) **Upset scenario:** Crash outrage fades. PSOE's mobilisation campaign ("stop PP-Vox") consolidates the left-wing vote from Frente Amplio, and debates go well for Sánchez. Then a 2023-style late PP underperformance, plus a polling miss of 5 or more points, gives PSOE the most votes. A Vox first place would need roughly a 12-point swing, which is extremely unlikely.

**Reasoning:** I start from the base rate, which gives essentially all probability to PP or PSOE, and the polls, which give a solid PP lead. I anchor on Polymarket. A 6-point lead with 26 days left and a typical Spanish lead error of about 3 to 4 points implies roughly a 10 to 13% chance that PSOE comes first. That is consistent with the market, so I do not move away from it. I keep small tails for Vox and other parties.
